title: Implement Copy-on-Write
hints: `isKnownUniquelyReferenced(&storage)` tells you whether anyone else shares your buffer.
Keep items in a private class; before mutating, copy the storage if it's shared (and count the copy).
jsBridge: Copy-on-write is how Swift arrays can be value types without copying on every assignment: shared storage plus `isKnownUniquelyReferenced` before mutating. Immutable.js and Immer do structural sharing to get a similar effect in JS.

compass.q: Immer gives you "mutate a draft, get a new object". How is Swift CoW similar, and how is it different (no proxies, reference-count based)?
Why must the storage be a `final class` for `isKnownUniquelyReferenced` to work?
Your own structs don't get CoW automatically. When should a big struct implement it?
Passing a 10k-element array to a function and mutating it inside: how many copies happen?
